static_traits.name: Lin Na
static_traits.social_status: Has friends to talk with, but has not yet discussed this negative belief with them; friendships are somewhat affected by avoiding film invitations or expressing negativity toward new films
static_traits.medical_history: No experience of similar psychological problems; no prior psychotherapy history; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Calm tone, clear thinking, able to self-reflect, good cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: I have long loved watching movies, but recently I have formed the belief that 'all future movies will be bad,' leading to anxiety and avoidance when new films are discussed or movie outings are planned, affecting my social life and enjoyment of movies.
basic_info.core_demands: Negative beliefs about future films have begun to affect social life and once-enjoyed activities, so the client seeks counseling to resolve this problem and restore enjoyment of watching films.

core_beliefs: Future experiences often tend to be disappointing
Positive expectations are unreliable; best to expect the worst to avoid disappointment

special_situations.event: When discussion about upcoming movies arises
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have expectations for a new film, I am more likely to be disappointed and waste time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: In discussions, emphasizing negative possibilities, lowering expectations for self-protection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will all be terrible; I will definitely be disappointed.

special_situations.event: Planning a movie night with friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the movie is bad, I will spoil everyone's mood and appear very uninteresting
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids participating or expresses negative views in advance to avoid being blamed
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will drag down everyone's mood; the evening will be awful.

special_situations.event: Receiving a movie invitation from a friend
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one or two movies are bad, it means movies in the future will basically all be bad
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Better not go, it will be bad anyway, going is a waste of time.

special_situations.event: At social occasions, talking about new releases and upcoming films
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not imagine the worst, I will bear greater disappointment in reality
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing on listing aspects where the movie might go wrong, avoiding positive information
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As soon as I think of all the places that could go wrong, I feel it will definitely be terrible.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to enjoy watching films again and relax with friends, and be accepted
core_conflict.fear: Fearing experiencing disappointment, worrying about affecting others' emotions and being seen as a spoilsport
defense_goal: Reducing the possibility of disappointment and embarrassment by anticipating the worst and avoiding watching movies

object_relations.self_representation: A person who worries about spoiling the fun and easily disappoints others
object_relations.object_representation: The other party is someone easily affected by my negative emotions, expecting me to match the atmosphere

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When friends talk about new films or extend movie invitations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes that if they take part everyone will be disappointed, or that the film is bound to be bad (treating the negative outcome as certain)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: States in a calm, objectified tone that 'films nowadays are all poor quality' and 'going would mostly be a waste of time', reducing emotional expression and tactfully declining invitations.

manifestations: A once-beloved film-watching activity becomes lacking in compose meaning and enjoyment
Forms blanket negative expectations about future films, weakening interest and engagement
outcomes: Increased alienation from interests and sense of hollowness
Anxiety about and avoidance of movie-watching-related situations

manifestations: Feeling out of place when friends talk about new films

exception_events.target_problem: When discussing or planning film watching with family or friends, the client usually expects the film to be bad, becomes anxious, and chooses avoidance or negative expressions.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once, she reluctantly watched a film with family, originally thinking it would be bad, but the actual viewing experience was 'quite good'; she felt surprised and realized that her negative expectations are not always accurate.
exception_events.reason: Different context / support: family accompanied and watched together; different approach: this time the client chose to actually go and watch rather than avoid; therefore a positive outcome different from before occurred.

positive_force: Long-standing love of watching films, a foundation of positive interest
Having social support such as friends and family available to use
Able to notice and reflect on own negative expectations (acknowledges being 'proven wrong' by positive experience)
Willing to try methods such as reality testing, recording, and gradual exposure
negative_force: Cognitive biases of catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and predicting the future
Avoidance behavior formed to avoid disappointment
Worrying excessively about 'spoiling the fun' in social situations; tends toward self-blame
Positive experiences are ignored, attention biased toward negative information, maintaining anxiety and avoidance

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids film-related activities and shows anxiety and negative speech when new films are mentioned
antecedent: Planning a movie night with friends
Receiving a movie invitation from a friend
target_behavior.core_reason: Influenced by thinking of catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and fortune telling, worrying about disappointment and wasting time, and fearing that affecting others' moods will make them be seen as a spoilsport.
target_behavior.function: Escaping anticipated disappointment and social awkwardness in the short term, temporarily reducing current anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social and leisure participation, film-watching enjoyment dropped markedly, negative beliefs reinforced, anxiety and avoidance maintained
